title: The Best Reference Anyone Can Receive or Give
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article dissects the unwritten formula most professional references follow, a formula so predictable that it fails to distinguish truly exceptional people from everyone else. The author contrasts this routine pattern with rare, unequivocal endorsements that flatly state someone should be hired or chosen without qualification. These rule-breaking references, the piece argues, carry outsized influence precisely because they depart from the expected script, and both the people who give and receive them earn added credibility as a result.
points: Most professional references follow a predictable script that praises strengths and softens a minor weakness.
That predictability makes ordinary references poor tools for distinguishing exceptional people.
Rare, unequivocal endorsements that flatly recommend hiring someone break from the usual code.
Because they're so uncommon, these direct endorsements carry disproportionate weight with decision-makers.
quotes: After serving and receiving many references, leaders soon learn there is an unwritten code to reference-making.
The reference that truly stands out is unusual because it is rarely true.
Endorsers, either by voice or writing, generally follow the same pattern. They establish how well they know the person and highlight the superlative qualities the person has demonstrated.
Leaders who give or receive a reference that flat out suggests the choice that should be made regarding the person wildly shake the tree.
Uncommon conviction, given or received, moves people to action.
